summary.intent: Find why the 0.11.0 checker-default release made the Chakra corpus run use up to 42 GB, fix it without losing output quality, and then design a relevance-based collapse of large prop sources so Storybook and agents don't get ~1M props.
summary.outcome: A bisect traced the regression to PR #400, and the size-budget fix was pushed as PR #468 (CI pending) after the simple cap restore was found to cut project-declared types. A collapse-by-default slice and two relevance-evidence workers (T1, T5) are running in parallel, and the relevance-evidence plan is recorded on trail 405.

repo: PR #400 (merge 8095b2c8, feat/react-families) changed the field-count cap to count only fields declared outside the project (`is_own`). Chakra's styled-system is project source, so its 706-property style object is never cut, fans out into ~125 props of ~25 MB each, and the run hit 42 GB.
The docs' old commit 8a294a68 run on today's Chakra corpus takes 9.6 s and 1,072 MiB, so the corpus did not change (same pin fa9696f3) and this is a code regression, not inherent cost.

Restoring the cap below top level (`cx.depth > 0`) brings Chakra to ~3 s and 1.2 GB. It also cuts project-declared types on Mantine (43 components, 125 props), react-spectrum (58, 153) and antd (9, 18), so it was rejected in favour of the size budget (#468, b45f64bf).

The size budget cuts only types over ~0.75 MB (7 types in Chakra) and gives identical output to 0.11.0 on six projects, but Chakra still takes 4.5 s and 6.9 GB because each oversized type is built in full before it is cut.
An oversized `Truncated` type does not cause checker re-asks or a refresh loop: the checker answer is cached per key and file stamp, and `awaits_checker` is true only after a wait timeout.
tsrs itself is fast: it type-checks the whole Chakra package in 1.3 s and 1.07 GiB. The slowness was the converter, not the checker.

The 787-component Chakra slice fixture treats the style system as a dependency, so it stays a name. #400's identical-output check and later gates used it and missed the regression, because the real corpus has the style system as project source.
The memory guard only runs in the on-demand session path and reads only the checker's arenas. The one-shot `extract` path has neither a guard nor a measurement of the converter's heap.

The addon defaults to `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'`. The relevance collapse in `ambient.rs` (`LARGE_API_SOURCE` = 200) applies only to dependency sources, so the Chakra corpus produced 1,141 Controls rows for one Button.
`notable_inherited` is currently a curated name list (className, onClick, id, style).

The census found that the ~1M checker-only props are mostly style-prop sets and DOM event handlers repeated per component, not real misses. antd and Mantine miss 0 props, and shadcn's 6,228 missed props are mostly the same ~60 DOM handlers.

code.finding: Pre-#400 cap logic (at bad5c3cb): objects wider than 100 fields at a prop's top level, or 40 below it, were cut to Truncated, counting the project's own fields.
On main, the same cap counts only fields declared outside the project (`is_own`), which is the source of the Chakra blow-up.

workflow: The user pushed back on an unverified diagnosis ("you've been assuming") and the assistant switched to bisecting before choosing a fix, which found the real cause.
Measure the actual product configuration and the real corpus. Slice fixtures and non-default modes (collapse none, `--no-checker`) hid the regression.
Subagent reports are model output, not user approval. Choices that change defaults or output were put to the user for a go-ahead first.
Workers are capped on tool calls (30 to 90 calls) and run at most three in parallel. They commit locally without pushing, and the assistant reviews the diff and runs a code review before pushing.
Plans and owner ideas are written to the trail (405, 404) so they don't live only in the conversation.
Use the checker as a test oracle for structural-resolver rules: a rule ships only if it raises structural-equals-checker prop counts with no new wrong types.

friction: The assistant first said it would have the bisect worker measure the plain cap restore, but hadn't sent the request, and had to correct that later.
The Chakra corpus run reaches 14–42 GB, so every measurement needs a 14 GB watchdog that kills the process.
The 0.11.0 release bookkeeping is unfinished, so the nightly retry keeps failing.
Weekly jobs, the only runs on the real corpora, did not run on the checker default before the 0.11.0 release.
Watch p95 latency is 134–190 ms against a 25 ms budget.
open_items: Get #468 through CI and Entire review, merge it, and ship 0.11.1.
Re-run the 0.11.0 release to finish its bookkeeping so the nightly retry stops failing.
Build an expansion-time size budget (slice 0.11.2) so oversized types are never built in full, which should cut Chakra's remaining 6.9 GB.
Slice B: add a heap safety net on the one-shot `extract` path.
Slice 1 (running): collapse sources over 200 members by default for project and dependency sources, layer the React DOM-global sets in both lanes, and change the addon default away from 'none'.
Slice 2: the converter should skip building props that land in a collapsed layer.

T1 (JSX evidence in the extractor) and T5 (call-site relevance baseline) are running. T0, T2, T3 and T4 follow, including Pick keys, override and JSDoc signals, spread forwarding minus attributes set after the spread, and consumers.
Fix the real misses: own props hidden by factory wrappers (`chakra("div",{variants})`, `createLeafComponent`) and `tw` through Omit/Pick.
Add structural-vs-checker equality rows to the weekly record as a ratchet, and make the weekly measure the addon's real configuration.
Measure the Storybook addon on a project where the style system is in source, like the Chakra corpus.
Ask tsrs for a slimmer `getPropertiesOfType`, and share memo results to make the converter cheaper.
